evidence: Workbook #35: 'At least one criterion proves the product's defining behavior works, and (where stateful) that state survives a reload / re-auth and is server-backed where required. (Server-backed != same-origin - network is public.)'; Internal sheet repeats it; skill reference quality-checks.md:145-147 says the same. (1) Defining behaviour graded: the brief's core is multi-user pipeline moves without trampling plus conversations. Functional judge.toml grades one-stage moves (hro_move_one_stage w1.5), stale-move refusal naming who (hro_stale_refused w2.5), all-or-none bulk moves (hro_bulk_all_or_none w2), undo/undo conflicts (hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict w2 each), live board within 15 s (hro_live_board w2.5), message exchange (hro_msg_exchange), per-person unread (hro_unread_counts w2). Polish grades update-preserves-work (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread w3 each). (2) Server-backed, not same-origin: functional/prompt.md:11 and polish/prompt.md:11 gate requires a job and card created as a Recruiter to be read by the Observer in a browser.newContext() independent context and says 'A reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent ... a browser-only save fails this check'. Order is re-read by Mei Lin in independent contexts (hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move, hro_undo_restores), add-candidate (hro_add_candidate), notes read by Aud (hro_notes), messages read by Tomas (hro_msg_exchange), Activity read by Aud (hro_activity). (3) Durability across restart: hro_restart (functional judge.toml:401-408) plus protocol D (functional/prompt.md:51) records jobs, per-stage order, notes, messages, activity and the seeded order/note, calls restart_app once, signs in again and requires all unchanged and 'the starting data is not loaded again'; 'A reload is not a restart'. hireops_rules.md:59 'Order survives a reload, a fresh sign-in and a restart' is thus covered by independent reads plus D. (4) Reload/re-auth durability of browser-local state the brief requires (instruction.md:7 'stays with that conversation when I look at another one, reload, or get signed out; when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it'): hro_drafts (judge.toml:366-372) covers switch/Board/reload and per-conversation separation; hro_pol_session_resume (polish judge.toml:54-60) covers ended session -> sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same-person resume and send (positive control), Mei on the same browser sees neither reply nor note draft, and Rafael's drafts survive Mei's visit. hro_msg_compose checks the sent text does not reappear after reload. Drafts may be browser-local by the public rule ('Where drafts are kept is yours', hireops_rules.md:174-175) so no hidden server-backing requirement is imposed. (5) Golden feasibility (scripted, not a judge run): raw-evidence-index hashes verified (workspace.cjs 9641026..., workspace.json a424b50..., server.log 6752f46...; server.js 4fc5d2c..., db.js 0367a73..., app.js 6ce330f..., threads.js 72371e8... all match the frozen task). workspace.json records passed groups 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding; live updates resume', 'session ended mid-draft: sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same person resumes and sends; another person sees no draft', 'drafts kept per conversation across switch and reload'. Golden db.js:24-53 persists users, sessions, jobs, applications, messages, reads, notes, activity, actions in SQLite; drafts are per-person localStorage (app.js:38-42). Weak apps considered: localStorage-only board -> fails the Observer independent-context gate (all binary 0); in-memory server store -> passes independent reads but fails hro_restart; drafts keyed by session token or cleared at sign-out -> fails hro_pol_session_resume, which matches the public requirement; drafts kept in global localStorage -> Mei sees them, fails. Conforming alternatives considered: server-stored per-user drafts, SSE/sockets/polling, different routes - none are penalised by these criteria. Residual observation (P3, not a fail of this row): no criterion re-reads per-person unread counts or seen marks after restart_app, so an app keeping read markers only in memory (seeded at boot) would lose no restart credit; the brief's 'keep new work across restarts' arguably includes them. Also an in-memory-store app forfeits only hro_restart (w1.5 of functional), a reward-magnitude matter for other rows. Risk=true because no configured judge run, reward-discrimination or ordering measurement exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'), so it is unmeasured whether the configured judge actually executes restart_app, independent contexts and the second-tab sign-out as written, and whether durability-broken apps are scored down in practice.
counterexample: No counterexample defeats the row. Bounded gap: an app storing per-person read markers in process memory (re-derived from seed at boot) passes every graded row, because hro_restart/protocol D do not re-read unread counts or seen marks after restart_app.
suggested_fix: Optional: add 'unread counts and seen marks per person' to the protocol D before/after record and hro_restart's unchanged list; and obtain a configured judge run plus a weak-app (in-memory store, global-localStorage drafts) discrimination run to retire the measurement risk.
